sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and JSON for kwes1245 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: No descriptive references at all: only Oosterwal 1961, Galis 1955 and van der Leeden 1954, each classed 'Wordlist or less'; classification Tor-Orya > Tor; no dialects listed. Local copy of hh.bib confirms every entry tagged [kwt] is overview/wordlist/socling.
No phonology at all; only classification (Foja Range > Orya-Tor > Tor > Tor Coast), four villages, ~2,000 speakers (1987), Ethnologue refs.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2024. Kwesten; Tor River; Tor Coast. New Guinea World (Santa Fe Institute), pages last modified 2024-06-25.
sources.note: Phonology section reads '[under construction]'. Its Sources list is the complete inventory of Kwesten data known to Usher: Galis 1955 (28 terms), Oosterwal 1961: 274-277 (67-79 terms) and 218-286 (kin terms), Voorhoeve 1975: 107 (39 terms after Anceaux), Smits & Voorhoeve 1994: 18-166 (comparative vocabulary after Oosterwal n.d.), Lee & Wambaliau 2004: 40-48 (239 terms) and 57-62 (21 sentences) for Kwesten of Holmafen and Arare; also 'Reimer, Songkilawand and Kana (1980) survey of Pantai Timur district (unobtained)'. No phonology, grammar or text source for Kwesten exists in his list.
sources.venue: New Guinea World (Santa Fe Institute), pages last modified 2024-06-25

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2007. Australasia and the Pacific. In Christopher Moseley (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, 425-577. London: Routledge.
sources.note: No Kwesten entry (not treated as endangered); Kwesten is only named as 'the larger TNGP, Tor language Kwesten' pressuring Keder, as 'the large Kwesten languages (P, TNGP, Tor) on the opposite coast' in the Anus entry, and in the map legend 'TOR LANGUAGES'. Nothing on stress/tone.
sources.venue: Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Bibliography to 1995: only indexes, checklist, atlas. No descriptive or phonological work on this language is indexed.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.6.2.2.11.1.5 'The Tor Family', pp. 413-414: six member languages, 'Kwesten is spoken along the coast and the immediate hinterland', a pronoun chart (Kwesten I akref, we anma/ana, you imi/ini); no phonological remarks on any Tor language; p. 876 one lexical comparison ('Kwesten, Tor Fam. has karkara' for 'dry').
sources.venue: New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. (144 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing. p. 38 entry '77. KWESTEN, IXa, ±500' gives villages (Ombe, Holmafin, Keder, Dabe, Takar, Betaf, Ansudu, Yamua) and sources (Galis 1955; Oosterwal 1961; Voorhoeve 1971); p. 107 is a 39-item comparative wordlist 'after Anceaux' in a unified non-phonemic orthography (note on p. 91) with no stress marking; 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the text.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU. (Map 1 legend p. 51 'Tor River Stock: Berrik, Dabe, Bonerif, Mander, Ittik/Ittik-Tor, Najdjbedj'; sec. on the Tami and Tor Stocks pp. 66-68: lexicostatistics and 14 Tami-Tor cognate sets with forms abbreviated BE Berik, BO Bonerif, I Ittik, IT Ittik-Tor, MA Mander, KE Kwesten, DA Dabe, NA Nainjbedj, taken from Oosterwal 1961.)
sources.note: Kwesten appears only as a source of comparative word forms in the Tami-Tor cognate sets (e.g. 'KE dun', 'KE safen', 'KE maf', 'KE dujis', 'KE toon', 'KE fon', 'KE masen'), unmarked for stress; no phonological commentary on any Tor language.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28)

sources.citation: Oosterwal, Gottfried. 1961. People of the Tor: A cultural-anthropological study on the tribes of the Tor territory (Northern Netherlands New-Guinea). Assen: Van Gorcum.
sources.note: Source of most later Kwesten wordlists (pp. 274-277 comparative terms; pp. 218-286 kin terms); an ethnographer's transcription, unlikely but possible to carry a remark on accent. Digitised at archive.org but access-restricted (lending).

sources.citation: Lee, Sang-Kem & Theresia Wambaliau. 2004. Kwanem languages survey report in Northeastern Papua, Indonesia. 88 pp. Manuscript, 'to appear in SIL Electronic Survey Reports'.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only substantial primary data on Kwesten (239-item wordlist pp. 40-48 and 21 sentences pp. 57-62 for Holmafen and Arare villages, per Usher's page citations); SIL survey reports normally state their transcription conventions and sometimes mark stress on the wordlist, so this is the one place a stress observation could exist. Apparently never published; not yet obtained even by Hammarström.
